title: Saving a part with its number unchanged is never refused as a duplicate
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have at the test location two active parts, part A and part B, on two different Part Library entries, whose part numbers differ only in hyphens or periods (such a pair comes from data saved before this release, or from the parts import).
  • Keep parts A and B as they are: this test changes only their Sell Price.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Type part B's part number in the Search box.
  2. Click the part B row.
  3. Replace the Sell Price with 25.00.
  4. Click Save.
  5. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  6. Click the part A row.
  7. Replace the Sell Price with 26.00.
  8. Click Save.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Part B is listed.

Step 2:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part B.

Step 3:

  • Sell Price reads $25.00.

Step 4:

  • The save goes through with no "already exists at this location" message.
  • The window closes and part B's row shows Sell Price $25.00.

Step 5:

  • Part A is listed.

Step 6:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens for part A.

Step 7:

  • Sell Price reads $26.00.

Step 8:

  • The save goes through with no "already exists at this location" message.
  • Part A's row shows Sell Price $26.00, and parts A and B keep their own part numbers.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S7-N5b: “S7-N3 and S7-N4 apply when a part is created and when its part number is changed. Saving a part with its number unchanged is never refused by them, even when the location already holds a part whose number matches it.”
  • Key Decisions: “A new part number already stocked at the location is refused, ignoring case and punctuation. This check stops a second copy of a part at one location. It runs when a part is created or its number is changed, never when a part is saved with its number unchanged. It is separate from linking, which stays exact.”
  • Story 7, context note: “Context note (S7-N7): in one rare case the import can still add a second part whose number differs from a stocked part only by punctuation, when the Part Library entry it matches is not the one stocked here. The duplicate merge tool cleans these up; the import does not refuse them.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
